Legal.title: Legal notice
Legal.lead: Who is behind Sello and what you can expect from its content.
Legal.unofficialBody: Sello is an independent project to help you prepare for Aptis ESOL General. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by the British Council, and it does not use its brand, logo or materials.
Legal.contentBody: All lessons, texts, audio and questions are original. They follow the format of the exam but do not copy official or third-party materials.
Legal.estimatesBody: The levels and scores shown in the app are our own estimates, not official results.
Legal.ownerBody: As required by article 10 of Spanish Law 34/2002 on information society services and e-commerce (LSSI-CE), these are the details of the website's owner:
Legal.hostingBody: The website is hosted by Vercel Inc. (440 N Barranca Ave #4133, Covina, CA 91723, USA).

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.lead: What data Sello keeps, what for and for how long.
Privacy.storedBody: Without an account everything is kept in your browser's local storage: your progress (attempts, scores and mistakes to review), your settings (theme, listening voice and speed, exam date, new cards per day), your flashcards, the mock exam in progress and Writing drafts. None of it is sent to any server.
Privacy.notStoredBody: We use no analytics or advertising cookies and no trackers. The only cookies are your session's, if you sign in (see the cookie policy).
Privacy.deleteBody: Without an account, you can export or delete your progress in Settings, and it also goes if you clear this site's data in your browser. With an account, clearing progress in this browser does not delete the cloud copy: delete the account for that.
Privacy.audioBody: In Speaking, the microphone is only used if you allow it when a session starts. Recordings stay in the page's memory and are deleted when you leave; they are only kept if you download them. The voice that reads the recordings is your own device's.
Privacy.hostingBody: Vercel, the hosting provider, logs technical data about each visit (such as the IP address and browser) to serve the website and protect it from abuse. The owner uses that data for nothing else.
Privacy.contactBody: Controller: {name}. For any privacy question, write to {email}.
Privacy.accountBody: An account is optional. If you create one, we keep your email (or the one Google gives us when you sign in with Google), your sign-up date and last sign-in, and copies of your progress, flashcards, exam date and mock exam in progress, so you can see them on all your devices. Writing drafts, voice settings and Speaking recordings are not uploaded.
Privacy.basisTitle: What for and on what legal basis
Privacy.basisBody: We use this data only to give you the account and sync your study: the legal basis is performing the service you ask for when you create the account (art. 6.1.b GDPR). We do not use it for advertising, sell it or pass it on, and we make no automated decisions about you.
Privacy.ageBody: To create an account you must be 14 or older (art. 7 of Spain's LOPDGDD). If you are younger, you can use Sello without an account.
Privacy.processorsBody: Supabase stores the account and synced data on servers in the European Union (Frankfurt). Vercel hosts the site and may process technical data about visits. If you sign in with Google, Google gives us your email to identify you. If you subscribe, Stripe Payments Europe processes the payment: it receives your name, email, billing address and payment method, which Stripe handles and Sello never sees, and keeps invoices for as long as tax law requires. Sello stores only your plan, its status, its dates and the Stripe identifiers. We have a data processing agreement with these providers.
Privacy.retentionBody: For as long as you have the account. When you delete it from your account page, your subscription is cancelled and your sign-in, your plan and all your synced data are erased, apart from the provider's temporary backups. Vercel's technical data is kept for the period that provider sets.
Privacy.rightsBody: You can access, correct, erase, restrict, object to and take away your data. You can do most of it yourself: export your progress in Settings and delete the account on your account page. For anything else, write to the contact below. If you think we have not answered properly, you can complain to the Spanish Data Protection Agency (www.aepd.es).

ExamGuide.formatLead: Five components. Each part has its own format, and Sello's trainers copy it.
ExamGuide.core: 25 grammar questions with 3 options and 25 vocabulary questions of 4 types.
ExamGuide.reading: Gapped sentences, putting a text in order, matching opinions and headings for a long text.
ExamGuide.listening: Specific information, matching speakers, opinions in a dialogue and attitude in a monologue. You can hear each recording once or twice.
ExamGuide.writing: Single words, a 20–30 word text, three 30–40 word answers and two emails: an informal one of 40–50 words and a formal one of 120–150.
ExamGuide.speaking: Personal questions, describing a photo, comparing two pictures and discussing an abstract topic after a minute to prepare.
ExamGuide.scoringBody: Each skill is scored from 0 to 50 and gets its own CEFR level. Scores can't be compared across skills, because the thresholds differ from one to another.
ExamGuide.coreTitle: Why Core can save a C
ExamGuide.coreBody: Grammar and Vocabulary are reported as a number from 0 to 50, with no level. But when a skill falls just below the threshold for a level, the Core score decides whether you get the higher level. Raising your Core score is the cheapest way to secure a C.
ExamGuide.estimateNote: Sello shows levels and scores estimated by the app. They are not official results.

ReadingPage.intro: The Reading paper lasts {minutes} minutes for all four parts, and you decide how to share them out. Here is what each part asks for, strategies to do it well and a trainer with original texts.
ReadingPage.examTime: App exam mode: {minutes} minutes for this part. The split is an app decision; the exam only sets the total.

reading-1.task: A short text (a note, an email, a notice) with {sentences} sentences. Each one has a missing word and you choose from {options} options.
reading-1.s1: Read the whole sentence before looking at the options: what comes after the gap often decides the answer.
reading-1.s2: Work out what kind of word is missing (verb, preposition, noun…) and rule out the options that are not.
reading-1.s3: Watch out for pairs that look alike in Spanish, such as make and do, or for and since.
reading-1.s4: This is the quickest part: do not get stuck, and save time for part 4.

reading-2.task: {tasks} texts of {sentences} sentences in the wrong order. The first one is already in place and you put the rest in order.
reading-2.s1: Look for words that point back to something earlier: pronouns (it, they, this), the before something already mentioned, such, these.
reading-2.s2: Linkers show the relationship: however introduces a contrast, as a result a consequence, finally an ending.
reading-2.s3: Find the pairs you are sure of first, then fit the rest around them.
reading-2.s4: When you finish, read the whole text through: if a sentence jumps out, check its position.

reading-3.task: {people} people give their opinion on the same topic. You decide who says each of the {statements} statements; some people match more than one.
reading-3.s1: Read the statements first so that you know which ideas you are looking for.
reading-3.s2: The statements paraphrase the texts: do not hunt for the same words, look for the same idea.
reading-3.s3: Notice the nuances: at first, I used to think, but or however change what the person really believes.
reading-3.s4: Use the highlighter to mark the sentence that supports each answer.

reading-4.task: A text of about {words} words in {paragraphs} paragraphs. You choose a heading for each one from {headings}: one is spare.
reading-4.s1: Read all the headings before you start and think about which idea each one sums up.
reading-4.s2: The main idea is usually in the first or last sentence of a paragraph; the examples in the middle are details.
reading-4.s3: Be suspicious of a heading that repeats a word from the paragraph: the right one usually sums up the idea in other words.
reading-4.s4: Start with the paragraphs you are sure of; with fewer options left, the hard ones get easier.

instructions.listening-1: Listen to the recording and choose the best answer.
instructions.listening-2: Four people speak. Choose what each person says; there are two options you do not need.
instructions.listening-3: Listen to the conversation and decide who expresses each opinion: the man, the woman or both.
instructions.listening-4: Listen to the speaker and answer the two questions about attitude, intention or opinion.

ListeningPage.intro: The Listening paper lasts {minutes} minutes and you hear each recording once or twice. Here is what each part asks for, strategies to do it well and a trainer with original scripts.
ListeningPage.examNote: App exam mode: each recording can be played {plays} times and there is no countdown. This is an app decision.
ListeningPage.voiceBody: The recordings are read aloud by the voices installed on your device, so quality varies. They are not the exam's recordings. You can choose voices and speed in Settings.

listening-1.task: A short message, monologue or dialogue and one question about a specific detail, with {options} options.
listening-1.s1: Read the question and the options before the audio starts: you know which detail to catch.
listening-1.s2: Numbers, days and times are often corrected in the recording; the final version is the right one.
listening-1.s3: Options repeat words from the audio on purpose. Choose the idea that fits, not the word you hear.
listening-1.s4: Use the second listening to check your answer, not to start from scratch.

listening-2.task: Four short monologues and {options} statements. You match each speaker with the idea that fits; two statements are left over.
listening-2.s1: Read all {options} statements first and underline the key idea in each.
listening-2.s2: The speaker paraphrases: listen for the idea, not the exact words.
listening-2.s3: If you miss one, move on and come back with the second listening.
listening-2.s4: Cross out each statement you use. What is left helps with the speaker you doubt.

listening-3.task: A conversation between a man and a woman and {statements} statements. For each one you decide whether the man, the woman or both say it.
listening-3.s1: While you listen, note M, W or both next to each statement.
listening-3.s2: Choose both only if each person expresses the idea. One speaker agreeing with a nod or an 'mm' is not enough.
listening-3.s3: Listen for changes of opinion: 'I used to think…', 'but', 'actually'.
listening-3.s4: Statements follow the order of the conversation, which helps you keep your place.

listening-4.task: A longer monologue and {questions} questions about attitude, intention or opinion, with {options} options each.
listening-4.s1: These questions are about how the speaker feels, not about facts: listen to tone and word choice.
listening-4.s2: Words like 'unfortunately', 'I'll admit' or 'surprisingly' show attitude.
listening-4.s3: A speaker can praise one thing and criticise another; the question asks about the overall view.
listening-4.s4: After answering in study mode, read the clues in the transcript to learn what to listen for.

instructions.writing-1: Answer the five messages with short replies of 1 to 5 words.
instructions.writing-2: Write a short answer in full sentences, 20 to 30 words.
instructions.writing-3: Answer the three chat questions, 30 to 40 words each.
instructions.writing-4: Read the notice and write two emails: an informal one to a friend and a formal one to the person in charge.

trainer.savedSummary: You ticked {correct} of {total} criteria. Your text has been removed from this device.
trainer.stopwatchLabel: Time spent against the recommended time:

writing-1.s1: A word or a short phrase is enough: you do not need a full sentence.
writing-1.s2: Answer exactly what you are asked; a logical answer beats a long one.
writing-1.s3: Check your spelling: in such short answers every word counts.
writing-1.s4: Do not go over 5 words and do not leave any message unanswered.

writing-2.s1: Write full sentences with a subject and a verb, even though the text is short.
writing-2.s2: Answer every point in the prompt, even with one sentence each.
writing-2.s3: Link your ideas with simple connectors (because, so, but) instead of loose sentences.
writing-2.s4: Stay between 20 and 30 words and check your verb tenses at the end.

writing-3.s1: Answer each question separately, in the tone of the chat: friendly but correct.
writing-3.s2: Give your opinion and support it with a reason or an example.
writing-3.s3: Vary your structures: a concession or an emphatic sentence lifts the level.
writing-3.s4: Share your time between the three answers so you finish the last one.

writing-4.s1: Write the informal email first: it is short and helps you order your ideas.
writing-4.s2: Really change register: contractions and phrasal verbs in the informal email; no contractions and polite formulas in the formal one.
writing-4.s3: In the formal email, state your reason in the first sentence, give reasons and suggest at least one solution.
writing-4.s4: Leave time to check the formal email: it is the longest and hardest text in this part.

writing-1.task: All five replies answer what was asked.
writing-1.organisation: Each reply has between 1 and 5 words.
writing-1.register: The replies sound natural in an informal conversation.

writing-2.task: I answered every point and wrote 20 to 30 words.
writing-2.organisation: The ideas are linked with connectors, not loose sentences.
writing-2.language: I use full, correct sentences with some precise vocabulary.
writing-2.register: The tone suits a club form or profile.

writing-3.task: All three answers respond to their question in 30 to 40 words.
writing-3.organisation: Each answer gives an idea and supports it with a reason or an example.
writing-3.language: There is a range of structures (concessions, conditionals, emphatic sentences) and few errors.
writing-3.register: The tone is that of a chat between members: friendly but correct.

writing-4.task: Both emails deal with the announced change and meet the word ranges.
writing-4.organisation: There is a greeting, clear paragraphs and a sign-off, and the ideas are well linked.
writing-4.language: I use a range of structures and vocabulary with few errors.
writing-4.register: The informal email sounds friendly and the formal one is polite, with no contractions.

task.writing-1: Five short messages from a club or community. You answer each one in 1 to 5 words.
task.writing-2: A form or profile with one personal question. You write 20 to 30 words in full sentences.
task.writing-3: Three questions from other members in a chat. You answer each one in 30 to 40 words.
task.writing-4: A notice about a change. You write an informal email to a friend (40–50 words) and a formal one to the person in charge (120–150 words).

instructions.speaking-2: Describe the picture and answer two more questions. You have 45 seconds for each one.
instructions.speaking-3: Compare the two pictures and answer two more questions. You have 45 seconds for each one.
instructions.speaking-4: Read the three questions. You have 1 minute to prepare and 2 minutes to answer all three together.

structure.speaking-1: Direct answer → a reason → a personal example.
structure.speaking-2: Overview → details (front, back) → speculation (might, looks as if) → your opinion.
structure.speaking-3: What they share → the differences (whereas, by contrast) → speculation → your preference and why.
structure.speaking-4: Experience (what, when, where) → how you felt → the general question with both sides → conclusion.

trainer.reviewTitle: Listen to yourself and compare with the models
trainer.checklistNote: Listen to your recordings, compare them with the models and tick what you achieved. This is the app's own rubric, not the official scale, and it gives no exam score.
trainer.savedSummary: You ticked {correct} of {total} criteria. Your recordings are deleted when you leave this session.

speaking-1.s1: Answer straight away and get to the point: 30 seconds go very fast.
speaking-1.s2: Add a reason and an example so you do not stop after one sentence.
speaking-1.s3: Use the time you have, but it is fine to finish a little early.
speaking-1.s4: Speak naturally: this part does not need fancy vocabulary.

speaking-2.s1: Start with an overview of the picture, then move on to the details.
speaking-2.s2: Speculate about what you cannot see for sure: might, could, it looks as if.
speaking-2.s3: In the other two questions, link the topic to your own experience.
speaking-2.s4: If your mind goes blank, use a phrase to buy time and carry on.

speaking-3.s1: Really compare: say what they share and how they differ, rather than describing each picture separately.
speaking-3.s2: Vary your comparison language: whereas, while, by contrast, far more.
speaking-3.s3: When you choose an option, give at least two reasons.
speaking-3.s4: Speculate about the people and their feelings to lift the level.

speaking-4.s1: Use the minute of preparation to note key ideas, not full sentences.
speaking-4.s2: Answer the three questions in order and link them into one talk.
speaking-4.s3: In the abstract question, present both sides before giving your opinion.
speaking-4.s4: Share out the 2 minutes: do not spend all your time on the story.

speaking-1.task: I answered all three questions with a reason or an example.
speaking-1.fluency: I spoke without long pauses for nearly all the time.
speaking-1.language: I used correct tenses and some precise vocabulary.
speaking-1.pronunciation: I am easy to understand when I listen back.

speaking-2.task: I described the picture and answered the other two questions.
speaking-2.fluency: I moved from the overview to the details and linked my ideas.
speaking-2.language: I speculated (might, could, looks as if) and used varied vocabulary.
speaking-2.pronunciation: I am easy to understand and my intonation sounds natural.

speaking-3.task: I compared the two pictures and answered the other two questions.
speaking-3.fluency: I organised the comparison and gave reasons for my choice.
speaking-3.language: I used varied comparison language and few repeated structures.
speaking-3.pronunciation: I am easy to understand and stress the key words well.

speaking-4.task: I answered all three questions in my two-minute turn.
speaking-4.fluency: I spoke continuously and linked the three answers.
speaking-4.language: I used complex structures (concession, conditionals, emphatic sentences) with few errors.
speaking-4.pronunciation: I am easy to understand throughout the turn.

SpeakingPage.intro: The Speaking paper lasts about {minutes} minutes and has four parts, from personal questions to a two-minute turn on an abstract topic. Here is what each part asks for, strategies and a trainer that records your answers and compares them with B2 and C models.
SpeakingPage.privacyTitle: Your voice never leaves your browser
SpeakingPage.privacyBody: Recordings stay in this page's memory: they are not uploaded anywhere or saved on the device, and they are deleted when you leave the session. If you want to keep one, press “Download”. The microphone is only requested when you start a session.
SpeakingPage.micBody: Record 3 seconds and listen back to check everything works before you practise.
SpeakingPage.noMarking: Sello does not mark your speaking: you listen to yourself, compare with the models and assess yourself with the app's own rubric, not the official one.

task.speaking-1: Three personal questions. You have 30 seconds for each answer.
task.speaking-2: One picture: you describe it and answer two related questions. You have 45 seconds for each one.
task.speaking-3: Two pictures: you compare them and answer two related questions. You have 45 seconds for each one.
task.speaking-4: One picture and three questions on an abstract topic. You have 1 minute to prepare and 2 minutes to answer all three together.

SpeakingPage.examNote: In the app's exam mode the question is read by one of your device's synthetic voices. If there is no voice, you get 5 seconds to read it before the time starts.

Placement.introBody: About 20 minutes to estimate your level in Core, Reading and Listening. The questions go from easier to harder, and you will not see the answers until each section ends.

sections.core: Core: 15 Grammar questions and 10 Vocabulary questions.
sections.reading: Reading: one task from part 1 or part 3.
sections.listening: Listening: three short part 1 recordings and one from part 2, each played twice at most.

Placement.introNote: Each section is saved as an exam-mode attempt, so your dashboard fills up as soon as you finish. You can take the test again whenever you like.
Placement.estimateNote: This is the app's rough estimate from a few questions, not an official score. It gets sharper as you practise.
Placement.notEstimated: Writing and Speaking are not estimated yet: do one task of each to get your level.

Mock.setupBody: The full exam with the real time for each component. Take it all at once or choose components, and carry on later if you close the page.
Mock.setupNote: If you reload in the middle of a section, the clock keeps running from its start: no time is given back. That section's answers are lost, except your Writing texts.
Mock.inProgress: Mock exam in progress. It is saved at the end of every section.
Mock.discardConfirm: Abandon this mock exam? The sections you finished stay in your progress.
Mock.estimateNote: Share of right answers and the app's estimated level, not an official score: the conversion to the exam's 0–50 scale is not public. Writing and Speaking come from your self-assessment.
Mock.gvBody: In the exam, Core has no level of its own, but it can decide the result when a skill falls just below a level. A good Core result helps those skills go up.

Terms.title: Terms of use
Terms.lead: The rules for using Sello and having an account.
Terms.whatBody: Sello is an independent website for practising Aptis ESOL General. It is not a service of the British Council or any examining body, and it does not guarantee any result in the official exam.
Terms.accountBody: Creating an account is optional and free. You must be 14 or older and give true details. You are responsible for your password. You can delete the account at any time from your account page.
Terms.useBody: Use Sello to study. Do not try to access other people's accounts, overload the service, extract its content in bulk or get around its security measures.
Terms.contentBody: Sello's lessons, texts and questions are original and belong to its owner. You may use them for your own study, but not copy or redistribute them without permission.
Terms.liabilityBody: Levels and scores are our own estimates. Sello is provided as is, with no guarantee of continuous availability, and we will take reasonable care of your data. This does not limit the rights the law gives you as a consumer.
Terms.plansBody: The B1, B2 and C1 plans are paid monthly or yearly, with VAT included in the price, and renew automatically until you cancel. You can cancel at any time from your account (Stripe's portal) and keep access until the end of the paid period. Upgrading is immediate and prorated; downgrading or cancelling takes effect at the end of the period. When a plan ends or goes down, your progress is kept, but content above your plan's level locks again. By paying you ask for immediate access to digital content and accept losing the 14-day right of withdrawal (article 103 m of Spain's consumer law). If you delete your account, the subscription is cancelled at once and the current period is not refunded.
Terms.changesBody: We may update these terms, and any change date will be shown here. They are governed by Spanish law.

Cookies.title: Cookie policy
Cookies.lead: Which cookies Sello uses and why we do not need to ask your permission.
Cookies.noneBody: If you do not sign in, Sello sets no cookies. Your theme, language and progress are kept in the browser's local storage, which is not a cookie and does not leave your device.
Cookies.sessionBody: Supabase keeps your session in cookies (names that start with 'sb-' and end in '-auth-token'). They are technical, strictly necessary, first-party cookies that keep you identified and they last until you sign out or delete them.
Cookies.consentBody: Strictly necessary technical cookies need no consent, which is why there is no banner. We use no analytics, advertising or third-party cookies. If we ever add them, we will ask your permission first.
Cookies.controlBody: Sign out from your account page or clear this site's cookies in your browser. You will be signed out and Sello will keep working in this browser.
